method: Both original PNGs were opened before consulting any modern geometry. Inventory comes from those pixels; no answer key was consulted.

sourceFacts.observation: One upright cylindrical bottle, projected oval open mouth, two long sides and rounded lower contour. The opening is above the coated lower region. Glass separates the inner and outer conducting surfaces.

A dark projected oval is visible inside the vessel in its upper-middle region, below the mouth. A short rear vertical interior edge is visible near the mouth. Its right/front edge stays inside the outer vessel contour.
The lower vessel has dark outer side bands and a rounded bottom boundary, with a broad light front region. The outer conducting coating reaches the side toward the discharger's lower ball.
A vertical conducting rod passes through the mouth, reaches the interior conductor, and has a small round terminal above the bottle. It is not a liquid column or a second bottle.

A bowed upper conducting arm rises from the upper terminal area, arches above the mouth, and descends to a right-side joint. The raster does not justify an added visible spark or calibrated upper contact gap.

A second curved arm leaves the same joint, bows downward/left and ends in a small round tip beside the outer coating. The lower ball remains distinct from the outer vessel edge; do not fill that clearance with a wire.
The two arms share one joint to the right of the bottle's mouth. One thick straight handle projects to the upper right from this joint. No hand, person, stand, battery or charging leads appear.

uncertainties: The upper arm touches or nearly touches the terminal in the coarse scan; show its approach without inventing a numbered gap or a discharge event.
Black fills and narrow contours are projected foil structure, not a measured dielectric thickness.
fig-158.safety: Historical apparatus identification only. No procedural steps, person repeating the experiment, toxic liquid, added hazard experiment or worked solution.

sourceFacts.observation: Two separated, upright parallel plate strokes in one frame; the left plate is negative and the right positive. Both have the same projected length.
One short horizontal lead protrudes outward from the left plate and one from the right plate, at approximately the same middle height. They are unconnected outside the diagram.
Six minus marks are arranged vertically just inside the left plate.
Six plus marks are arranged vertically just inside the right plate, corresponding to the negative rows.
The outer upper labels are -|q| beside the left plate and +|q| beside the right plate. These are signed plate charges, not extra point charges.

Six straight, approximately equally spaced horizontal field arrows span the same gap, all pointing LEFT, from the positive right plate to the negative left plate. They are perpendicular to both plates.
An E with the conventional vector accent is above the upper field line. It denotes the total gap field, not an E/2 label or a force arrow.
